conflict_topics: disputed seat at a full two-seat table
who may occupy the seat immediately (timing/priority)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete practical reasons (hot bowl will spill; hot food; not wanting to carry the bowl) which ground their positions.
Agents request/offer concrete temporal information ('roughly how long', 'I'll be finished very soon') enabling resolution.
Minor repetition: B repeats 'almost done' assurances twice (Turns 5 and 11) but this is brief and functional.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent B committed to free the seat when finished ('I'll be finished very soon. You can have the seat next.' — Turn 8). Agent D accepted waiting ('Okay, I'll wait.' — Turn 9). Agent A accepted waiting and agreed to stand off the aisle ('... fine, I'll wait. I'll stand just off the aisle. Please let me sit as soon as you're done.' — Turn 10). Thus parties agreed that B would keep the seat until done and others would wait rather than attempting to take it immediately.
position_change_notes: Agent B consistently retained the seat until finished and repeatedly assured others they would free it soon (Turns 5, 8, 11).
Agent A softened their initial demand and conceded to waiting ('... fine, I'll wait.' — Turn 10).
Agent D asserted a claim to be next (Turn 7) and accepted B's allocation and the decision to wait ('Okay, I'll wait.' — Turn 9).
Agent C acted as a mediator/facilitator asking for a time estimate but did not press a competing claim (Turn 4 and 6).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 (Agent A): '...can I sit there?' vs Turn 2 (Agent B): 'I sat here ... I can't give up the seat right now; I'll free it when I'm done.' — direct incompatible claims over the seat.
Turn 3 (Agent A) proposes moving the bowl or a time estimate; Turn 4 (Agent C) supports waiting or moving the bowl. Negotiation continues but B's refusal remains.

Turn 5 (Agent B): 'I can't put the open bowl on the table — it's hot and will spill ... I'm almost finished;' Turn 6 (Agent C) asks for a time estimate and asks A to stand aside. B still insists on staying; disagreement persists.

Turn 7 (Agent D) asserts a competing claim: 'I'd like the next free seat.' Turn 8 (Agent B) promises: 'I'll be finished very soon. You can have the seat next.' A new claimant appears and B assigns the next seat to D, so the situation becomes more contested.

Turn 9 (Agent D): 'Okay, I'll wait.' Turn 10 (Agent A): '... fine, I'll wait. I'll stand just off the aisle. Please let me sit as soon as you're done.' All parties explicitly accept waiting and B previously committed to free the seat soon (Turn 8), yielding a spoken agreement on who waits and that the seat won't be taken immediately.
Turn 11 (Agent B): repeats 'I'm almost done; I'll free the seat as soon as I'm finished.' Turn 12 (Agent A): 'Okay — I'll wait here.' No substantive conflict; prior agreement reiterated.
No public speech or observable action recorded; no new conflict introduced.
No public speech or observable action recorded; situation remains the settled waiting arrangement from earlier rounds.

substantive_insights: The core incompatibility was a practical constraint: B cannot safely move an open hot bowl, while A has hot food and needs a seat immediately.
Resolution was achieved via temporal sequencing and mutual waiting rather than reassigning immediate possession: B retains the seat until finished, others agree to wait.
A new claimant (D) appeared and B explicitly offered the next seat to D; A accepted waiting anyway, avoiding an immediate allocation dispute.
